title: Weil restriction of constants and Frobenius powers
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal F=(M,\theta)$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. For $e\geq1$, put $k_e=\mathbf F_{q^e}\subset k$ and $X_{0,e}=X_0\times_{k_0}k_e$. Under the canonical identification $X_{0,e}\times_{k_e}k\simeq X$, the geometric Frobenius of the extended base is $g_X^e$. The iterated Weil isomorphism
$$\theta^{[e]}=\theta\circ Lg_X^*\theta\circ\cdots\circ L(g_X^{e-1})^*\theta$$
defines a lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal F^{(e)}=(M,\theta^{[e]})$ on $X_{0,e}$.
For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, the identity on the underlying coefficient cohomology identifies
$$\bigl(H_c^r(X,\mathcal F^{(e)}),F_{q^e}\bigr)\simeq\bigl(H_c^r(X,\mathcal F),F_q^e\bigr)$$
as Frobenius modules, with compact cohomology as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. If a closed point $z\in X_{0,e}$ maps to $x\in X_0$, the local geometric Frobenius on the stalk of $\mathcal F^{(e)}$ at $z$ is conjugate to
$$F_x^{[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]}$$
with the local-operator convention of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. For every real $w$, if $\mathcal F$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then $\mathcal F^{(e)}$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ relative to $k_e$ [def-weil-punctual-weights]. No geometric connectedness or semisimplicity is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $g=g_X$ and let $g_e$ be the geometric Frobenius of $X_{0,e}\times_{k_e}k$. Under the canonical associativity identification of the two base changes, the affine formula for geometric Frobenius gives $g_e=g^e$. The pullback of a lisse sheaf along this identification is lisse. Starting with $\theta:Lg^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$, define
$$
\theta^{[e]}=\theta\circ Lg^*\theta\circ\cdots\circ L(g^{e-1})^*\theta.
$$
The iterated-Weil cocycle identity identifies the same composite for every decomposition of $e$, so $(M,\theta^{[e]})$ is a Weil sheaf over $k_e$; when $e=1$ this is the original sheaf. This construction is made at a finite coefficient stage and then transported to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ by the common-stage convention, so no semisimplicity or connectedness is used.

proof.text:
Let $C=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ and let $t$ be the compact-support transport along $g$ from the definition of geometric Frobenius on cohomology. The transport is natural in the coefficient complex, and the transport along $g^e$ is the successive composite $t^{[e]}=t_{Lg^{e-1*}M}\circ\cdots\circ t_M$; this is the composition law for the specified Frobenius transports, first at finite coefficient level and then after passage to the common $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ stage. Applying the categorical transport-power identity to the morphism $\theta:Lg^*M\to M$ gives
$$
(C(\theta)\circ t_M)^e=C(\theta^{[e]})\circ t^{[e]}.
$$
By the definition of the global geometric-Frobenius operator, the left side is $F_q^e$, while the right side is the operator $F_{q^e}$ for $(M,\theta^{[e]})$. Taking degree-$r$ cohomology proves the asserted identity on $H_c^r$.

proof.text: Let $z$ lie over the closed point $x$, and put $d=[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]$. Finite-field Galois theory identifies the residue extension with the degree-$d$ Frobenius orbit. In the stalk definition of local geometric Frobenius, one circuit at $x$ is the composite of the pullback/reparametrization transport with $\theta$; traversing the orbit $d$ times at $z$ inserts successively $\theta,Lg^*\theta,\ldots,L(g^{d-1})^*\theta$. The cocycle identity from Step 1 therefore identifies this return operator with $F_x^d$. Changing the chosen embeddings of either residue field only changes the displayed operator by conjugation, by the local-Frobenius conjugacy lemma. The same argument is valid at every finite coefficient stage and hence after scalar extension to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

proof.text:
Assume that $\mathcal F$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$. If $\alpha$ is an eigenvalue of $F_x$, the definition of purity gives $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_x^{w/2}$, where $q_x=|\kappa(x)|$. Step 3 says that the corresponding eigenvalues over $z$ are $\alpha^d$ (with multiplicities and conjugacy unchanged), while $q_z=|\kappa(z)|=q_x^d$. Hence
$$
|\iota(\alpha^d)|=|\iota(\alpha)|^d=q_x^{dw/2}=q_z^{w/2},
$$
which is precisely punctual purity of $\mathcal F^{(e)}$ relative to $k_e$. If a stalk is zero there are no eigenvalues, so the assertion is vacuous.

proof.text: All constructions are functorial in the underlying sheaf and use only the finite-field base-change identifications, so they do not require geometric connectedness, a choice of components, or semisimplicity. The cases $e=1$, the zero sheaf, and empty cohomology reduce to the defining identities and are covered.
